title: Files and Folders
about: Find files, read their types, and tell local files from cloud ones.

cards.prompt: `volcanoes.docx` is in `Science`, inside `School`, inside `Documents`. Order its **path**, biggest folder first.
cards.explanation: A path runs from the biggest folder inwards: `Documents > School > Science > volcanoes.docx`. The file comes last.
cards.hint: Folders are like boxes in boxes: start with the one that holds everything.
cards.nudge: Go from the biggest folder inwards; the file comes last.

cards.title: Extensions
cards.body:
The end of a file's name, after the **last** dot, is its **extension**. It tells the OS what kind of file it is.

`.jpg` is a photo, `.mp3` a song, `.mp4` a video. `.exe` is a **program**: opening it *runs* it, so only open ones you trust.

cards.prompt: Match each [[extension]] to the kind of file it marks.

pairs.right: A program that runs when opened

cards.explanation: `.mp3` is a song and `.mp4` a video: one letter apart. `.exe` is a **program**, so opening it *runs* it.
cards.hint: Think back to the list: photos, songs, videos and programs.
cards.nudge: `.mp3` and `.mp4` look alike but mark different things.

cards.prompt: Label what each file really is. Read to the **last** dot.
cards.explanation: `photo.jpg.exe` ends in **.exe**, so it's a program, whatever the `.jpg` in the middle says.
cards.hint: Only the [[extension]] after the **last** dot counts.
cards.nudge: Ignore anything in the middle; look only after the last dot.

cards.prompt: A website promised free holiday wallpapers. You clicked download.

steps.text: Your Downloads folder now has a new file: `photo.jpg.exe`. What is it?

choices.consequence: Only the **last** [[extension]] counts. The `.jpg` in the middle is a disguise.

choices.text: A program dressed as a photo
choices.consequence: Right. It ends in **.exe**, so opening it would run it.

steps.text: What do you do with it?

choices.text: Open it once, just to check
choices.consequence: Opening a program runs it, and it only takes one run for it to do harm.

choices.text: Send it to a friend to try
choices.consequence: Now your friend's device is at risk too.

choices.text: Delete it unopened, tell an adult
choices.consequence: The file is gone, and they can check nothing else came with it.

cards.explanation: `photo.jpg.exe` is a program in disguise, and some computers even hide the last extension. Delete it unopened and tell a parent, teacher or other adult you trust.
cards.hint: Read to the last dot: what happens when you open that kind of file?

cards.prompt: **The cloud** is a company's **server**: a computer you reach over the internet. Where is each file stored?

items.label: A song downloaded to play offline
A drawing saved to the laptop's storage
A shared doc you edit in a web browser
Emails in a web mail inbox
A game save kept in your online account

cards.explanation: Files you **downloaded** or **saved to the device** are in its storage. Files you reach **online** live on a company's servers.
cards.hint: Did you save it to the device, or do you reach it through a website or account?
cards.nudge: Downloaded or saved to the device means its storage; reached online means a server.

cards.prompt: You're on a plane with no Wi-Fi, and you want to work on your essay. It's saved **only in the cloud**.

choices.text: Yes: it's my file, so my laptop has it
choices.consequence: It lives on a company's server, not your laptop. With no internet, you can't reach it.

choices.text: Yes: cloud files reach you through the air
choices.consequence: The cloud isn't in the sky. It's a server in a building, and you can only reach it over the internet.

choices.text: No: I need the internet to reach its server
choices.consequence: Right. No internet, no essay. Time for the in-flight movie.

steps.text: Next time you fly, how can you work on it without Wi-Fi?

choices.text: Download a copy before the flight
choices.consequence: A copy in the laptop's storage opens anywhere, even on a plane.

choices.text: Save it to the cloud twice as a spare
choices.consequence: Both copies are still on the server. You need one on the laptop.

cards.explanation: Cloud files live on a company's [[servers|server]], so you need the internet to reach them. Keep a copy on your device when you'll be offline.
cards.hint: Where does a cloud-only file really live, and what do you need to reach it?

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- Folders hold files. The **path** is the route to a file.
- The **extension** after the last dot says what it is. `.exe` runs.
- **Cloud** files live on a server you reach over the internet.

That's the software side. Next module: fixing things yourself.
